title: Remembering Hiroshima/Nagasaki Bombings. 80 Years Later. NEVER AGAIN!
description:
Our procession commemorates the solemn and world-changing event of the first use of nuclear weapons in war on August 6, 1945. This act must never be repeated. In the current world of rising tensions and 9 countries now possessing nuclear weapons, we are at the brink of potential civilization-ending disaster. 

As UN Secretary General António Guterres said in June 2024 “Humanity is on a knife’s edge. The risk of a nuclear weapon being used has reached heights not seen since the Cold War. We need all countries to step up. But nuclear-weapon states must lead the way.”
     
Our Exhibit, Horror To Hope: Stepping Back from the Brink features a selection from The A-Bomb and Humanity, a set of 40 exhibition panels created by the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers Organizations, or Nihon Hidankyo. Comprising photographs, drawings, and first-hand accounts of survivors from the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings creators of this collection hopes to "arouse world public opinion for the elimination of nuclear weapons." 

The group was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2024–for “demonstrating through witness testimony that nuclear weapons must never be used again”. 

Horror to Hope also presents some of the history of anti-nuclear activism in Central New York, thereby creating solidarity between survivors and advocates across the world.The content is meant to confront the viewer with the reality of nuclear war, and to remind us that a future without nuclear weapons is only possible through the activism of people like us.

title: Community Outreach at County Outpatient Clinics: San Jose Group 1

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

description:
Hello, fellow activists in Santa Clara County!

I'm Cristina de la Fuente - a registered nurse who lives in San Jose and founder of Fund Healthcare, Not Billionaires, a grassroots movement uniting the caring residents of Santa Clara County to stay informed and protect as many lives as possible from the deadly federal cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.

I’m inviting fellow activists to join me in a critical community outreach effort to distribute healthcare information to patients of the Santa Clara Valley Health and Hospital System—a population deeply impacted by these severe cuts.

Volunteers will join me at the address provided to distribute literature with a brief explanation. We will go to multiple County outpatient clinics. Our goals are to encourage patients and staff to:

(1) Attend upcoming Town Halls and public events where Santa Clara County leadership will announce critical updates about public healthcare and safety-net services.

(2) Subscribe to the email list on www.FundHealthcareNotBillionaires.com to receive urgent updates and volunteer opportunities for community outreach and future mutual aid initiatives.

(3) Submit anonymous questions and real-life concerns related to the impact of severe federal cuts to public healthcare and social safety-net services. These will be shared (without identifying information) on our community advocacy website, www.FundHealthcareNotBillionaires.com. Responses from Santa Clara County leadership will be provided, including direct quotes and verified source links.

County clinics serve patients whose lives depend on uninterrupted care. This volunteer event is an educational outreach to empower our community members with life-saving information and ways to take action.

No experience is necessary — just bring compassion, patience, and a commitment to healthcare for all.

Sign up for one or more shifts to help protect people's lives in Santa Clara County.

title: Activism 101 with IndiMarin
description:
Democracy is under attack by the very people who are sworn to protect it. The solution? Experts on authoritarianism say that 3.5% of citizens are needed to successfully replace an authoritarian government. That means we need 12 million Americans to be actively engaged in this fight. In other words, we need YOU! And MANY other people just like you.

Since broad recruitment is crucial to the success of the Resistance, Indivisible Marin, along with our partners, is introducing a workshop designed for new activists. Our Activism 101 workshop introduces you to four ways you can contribute virtually to the Resistance movement.

At the workshop, you will choose from one of the four tactics listed below, and then join a breakout room with a mentor who will cover what you need to get started, provide a demonstration of the tactic, and offer a brief Q&A period. (Note: You will not be actively making calls or writing postcards at the workshop.) 

You will choose one of these four tactics and learn how to: 

Multiply your impact through relational organizing: Help reach the crucial 3.5% goal by reaching out to friends and encouraging them to join the effort. We will cover an easy toolkit with tips on reaching out 1:1 via open-ended conversations. We will also provide ideas for multiplying your impact by organizing your own gatherings and protests.

Write postcards to voters: Learn how to order your own supplies, scripts, and addresses. You’ll select from a variety of campaigns, including writing to voters in the upcoming Virginia elections or writing to voters in battleground congressional districts across the country with Republican representatives.

Make phone calls to voters: Phonebanking is one of the most effective methods we have to encourage civic participation! Also, today's phonebanking tools are easy to use and able to target Democratic voters. description:
Hello, fellow activists in Santa Clara County!

I'm Cristina de la Fuente - a registered nurse who lives in San Jose and founder of Fund Healthcare, Not Billionaires, a grassroots movement uniting the caring residents of Santa Clara County to stay informed and protect as many lives as possible from the deadly federal cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.

I’m inviting fellow activists to join me for an urgent community outreach effort to reach one of the most medically vulnerable populations in Santa Clara County: residents of long-term acute care (LTAC) facilities. These are people who often rely on ventilators, dialysis, feeding tubes, and round-the-clock nursing care—and who are now at serious risk due to devastating cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, and other safety-net services.

Volunteers will join me at the address provided to distribute literature with a brief explanation. We will go to multiple LTAC facilities. Our goals are to encourage the patients' family members and staff to:

(2) Subscribe to the email list on www.FundHealthcareNotBillionaires.com to receive urgent updates and volunteer opportunities for community outreach and future mutual aid initiatives.

(3) Submit anonymous questions and real-life concerns related to the impact of severe federal cuts to public healthcare and social safety-net services. These will be shared (without identifying information) on our community advocacy website, www.FundHealthcareNotBillionaires.com. Responses from Santa Clara County leadership will be provided, including direct quotes and verified source links.

Long-term acute care facilities serve patients whose lives depend on uninterrupted care. This volunteer event is an educational outreach to empower our community members with life-saving information and ways to take action.

No experience is necessary — just bring compassion, patience, and a commitment to healthcare for all.

Sign up for one or more shifts to help protect people's lives in Santa Clara County.
